payingUser: A self-managing landlord who owns a handful of rental units and walks them themselves at move-in and move-out, not an enterprise property manager whose employer chose Yardi.
paidUnit: One non-consumable unlock of unlimited units and PDF export without a watermark, bought once with no renewal.
momentOfPayment: After the landlord finishes one free unit walk with photos and taps Share or Export on the report; the free unit is fully usable, and the unlock is offered for a second unit or for PDF export without watermark.
distinctnessSentence: A crash-safe, no-account unit walk that keeps every photo through the report, compares move-in to move-out per unit, and shares a signed PDF from the phone — without RentCheck cloud camera failures or Yardi and Property Inspect employer logins.
day1RevenuePath: A landlord searching landlord inspection app or move in move out inspection installs the free one-unit walk, survives a full photo walk offline, taps export, and buys the 9.99 dollar unlock through Play Billing.

capabilities.note: billing collects the one-time unlock. ads stays off: a banner mid-walk over deposit evidence is hostile, and the enriched top ten on landlord inspection app declared zero ads.

permissions: CAMERA for TakePicture / ACTION_IMAGE_CAPTURE on the walk; POST_NOTIFICATIONS only if a reminder surface ships later (not required for the core walk). Photo Picker backfill needs no runtime permission. Share/export uses FileProvider and ACTION_SEND / ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT with no storage permission on modern Android.

archetypesRejected.revenueReason: Zero of the enriched top ten on landlord inspection app declared ads; money on the shelf is SaaS accounts and IAP unlocks. An interstitial over a deposit walk is hostile and would earn nothing at this session shape.
There is no consumable to re-sell: the landlord needs the same walk forever. Charging per PDF export is rent by another name and recreates the subscription anger this factory bans.
Shelf leaders that reach 10K–100K installs are free to download (RentCheck, myInspections, Property Inspect). A paid-upfront listing spends the free-walk funnel PropertyLog and RentProof already use.

Banned outright by the owner on 2026-10-01 and absent from ARCHETYPES. Named only because enterprise incumbents make it the natural B2B shape — which is exactly why this recipe targets the self-managing landlord with a one-time unlock instead.

assumptionsUnverified: That a self-managing landlord pays 9.99 once instead of Notes plus the Camera roll; no priced IAP amount was MEASURED on this shelf (myInspections / Property360 / PropertyLog declare IAP true with no dollar figure in enrich-market).

That unrated PropertyLog (1+ installs, IAP) and RentProof have not already absorbed the offline one-time buyers; PropertyLog's install floor is the discovery risk for this shape, not proof the job is empty.

Play fee arithmetic used by this plan (list 9.99): at ASSUMPTION 15 percent fee (first-$1M / new-install default in docs/monetization-strategy.md §2.2) net ≈ 8.49 per sale; at stress 30 percent fee net ≈ 6.99. Sales/month for ~100 dollars net: ≈12 at 15 percent, ≈15 at 30 percent. Sales/month for the factory illustrative 1000 dollars net: ≈118 at 15 percent, ≈144 at 30 percent. Kill floor 80 dollars / 60 days needs ≈9.4 unlocks at 15 percent (~11.4 at 30 percent).

Install-to-unlock conversion assumed near 2 percent (docs/monetization-strategy.md §4 band 1–3 percent, itself UNVERIFIED). At 800 installs and 2 percent ≈16 unlocks ≈136 dollars gross-of-refunds at 15 percent net, which clears the 80 dollar kill; at 1 percent ≈8 unlocks ≈68 dollars, which MISSES it.
The loudest pain on Yardi is enterprise users who cannot switch; whether the self-managing landlord feels the same photo-loss pain hard enough to pay is UNVERIFIED.
